How AI grows and what memory it needs at each step      Stage   is training    HBM demand sits at Extreme  Conventional DRAM  NAND SSDs  and even HDDs are High   Tape is Moderate   This is the heavy phase that first put HBM in the spotlight   Stage   is basic chatbot inference    Overall demand eases  HBM stays High  but DRAM  NAND  HDD  and tape drop to Moderate or Low   Once the model is trained  simple chat needs less raw resources   Stage   is advanced inference with long context  RAG  and reasoning   HBM returns to Extreme   NAND Flash and enterprise SSDs also hit Extreme   DRAM is High and HDDs Moderate  Longer contexts and retrieval pull far more data through the system   Stage   is agentic AI   This is the real shift   Conventional DRAM and NAND both go Extreme   HDDs rise to High   HBM remains High   Agents that plan  remember past steps  and use tools need large amounts of working memory and persistent storage  not just the absolute fastest chips   The simple takeaway is clear    Early AI mostly lifted HBM and high end DRAM   As systems move toward smarter agents  NAND SSDs and even hard drives become critical too  More data has to be stored  retrieved  and kept ready for longer periods   That puts companies tied to DRAM  NAND SSDs  HDDs  and the Korean memory makers squarely in the path of the next demand wave   AI is not a single boom   Each new stage pulls different parts of the memory and storage stack    We are already past pure training and basic chat  The next phase of advanced reasoning and agents looks set to broaden the lift across more of the stack

Copper is winning the AI data center race today but a handoff to light based chips will flip that by         Copper wiring moves data as electrical signals through metal  which is why it has powered every data center for decades  since it s cheap to manufacture  uses very little power  and is extremely reliable and easy to repair  The catch is physics because at extremely high speeds modern AI chips demand  electrical signals degrade fast as they travel through metal  so copper only works reliably over very short distances  typically     meters at     gigabit per second lane speeds  which happens to be almost exactly the width of a single server rack  That s precisely why copper still dominates connections between GPUs sitting inches apart inside the same rack today  a use case called scale up  while it already struggles more in scale out connections that stretch between racks across the data center floor   Optical  or light based  connections solve that distance problem because light signals traveling through fiber don t degrade the way electricity does over metal  so they can carry massive amounts of data across much longer distances without losing signal quality  Co packaged optics or CPO  takes this further by placing the optical engine directly onto the same chip package as the switch or GPU itself  rather than in a separate pluggable module  which cuts power consumption and latency even more  The chart s orange area growing over time represents this shift toward CPO steadily replacing copper as AI chips get faster and copper s usable range keeps shrinking

Copper is winning the AI data center race today but a handoff to light based chips will flip that by         Copper wiring moves data as electrical signals through metal  which is why it has powered every data center for decades  since it s cheap to manufacture  uses very little power  and is extremely reliable and easy to repair  The catch is physics because at extremely high speeds modern AI chips demand  electrical signals degrade fast as they travel through metal  so copper only works reliably over very short distances  typically     meters at     gigabit per second lane speeds  which happens to be almost exactly the width of a single server rack  That s precisely why copper still dominates connections between GPUs sitting inches apart inside the same rack today  a use case called scale up  while it already struggles more in scale out connections that stretch between racks across the data center floor   Optical  or light based  connections solve that distance problem because light signals traveling through fiber don t degrade the way electricity does over metal  so they can carry massive amounts of data across much longer distances without losing signal quality  Co packaged optics or CPO  takes this further by placing the optical engine directly onto the same chip package as the switch or GPU itself  rather than in a separate pluggable module  which cuts power consumption and latency even more  The chart s orange area growing over time represents this shift toward CPO steadily replacing copper as AI chips get faster and copper s usable range keeps shrinking

Copper is winning the AI data center race today but a handoff to light based chips will flip that by         Copper wiring moves data as electrical signals through metal  which is why it has powered every data center for decades  since it s cheap to manufacture  uses very little power  and is extremely reliable and easy to repair  The catch is physics because at extremely high speeds modern AI chips demand  electrical signals degrade fast as they travel through metal  so copper only works reliably over very short distances  typically     meters at     gigabit per second lane speeds  which happens to be almost exactly the width of a single server rack  That s precisely why copper still dominates connections between GPUs sitting inches apart inside the same rack today  a use case called scale up  while it already struggles more in scale out connections that stretch between racks across the data center floor   Optical  or light based  connections solve that distance problem because light signals traveling through fiber don t degrade the way electricity does over metal  so they can carry massive amounts of data across much longer distances without losing signal quality  Co packaged optics or CPO  takes this further by placing the optical engine directly onto the same chip package as the switch or GPU itself  rather than in a separate pluggable module  which cuts power consumption and latency even more  The chart s orange area growing over time represents this shift toward CPO steadily replacing copper as AI chips get faster and copper s usable range keeps shrinking

placed together on the front side of the chip  As process nodes shrink  however  competition between the two in an increasingly confined space exacerbates routing congestion and increases electrical resistance  leading to more severe IR drop  problems   Addressing these issues through backside power delivery typically requires substantial changes to transistor placement or cell structures   These challenges become more pronounced as process nodes shrink  Supplying power from the back side of the chip has generally required designers to give up parts of their existing cell libraries and design and a record    exhibition booths  Here is what I wanted everyone in the room to take away  Watch the video below to see the clip  Quantum runs on two clocks  One is R D  measured in qubits and bit error rate  The other is commercial  measured in investment  manufacturing capacity and speed to market  These two clocks report to different stakeholders  and the whole point of bringing the research community and the industrial community into the same building is to make them tick together   Why now  Because the money has changed character  Three of the world s largest economies are treating quantum as critical infrastructure with taxpayer money behind it  roughly  bn USD in the US alongside IBM s   bn commitment to manufacture quantum at home    bn in the EU Quantum Act over the next five years  and  bn GBP in the UK  On the private side  Quantinuum is heading to an IPO near    bn USD and Oxford Quantum Circuits  OQC  raised    m GBP  the largest round ever for a European quantum company   The technical progress is real  too  We are seeing error correction progress quickly  including demonstrations of correcting    logical qubits out of     But the most important signal came from two companies I spoke to before the event  QuiX Quantum in Enschede is building photonic quantum chips designed so the hardware naturally fits the customer s algorithm  particularly for quantum chemistry  Jelmer Renema  CSO  people are lining up at the door  Imran Khan  Managing Director of German CVQKD company  KEEQuant  building integrated photonics for quantum key distribution  put it more bluntly  the threat is real now  telecom operators need these chips in volume today  and we cannot wait for the threat to materialise  They have already run a    km carrier grade link between Berlin and Bonn  delivered as keys as a service   That is the shift  A few years ago  quantum capital was blue sky money  Today  every investor in the room is asking the same question  if I put money world in photonics  and     of that leadership has nothing to do with semiconductors  Ultrashort pulse lasers  laser cutting  and lens making  This is core to our strategic autonomy  and it is easy to forget when every headline is about chips  Chips Joint Undertaking matters  but photonics is far bigger than its semiconductor slice  The base is strong too  a deep university landscape  a Photonics   community of       members  mostly SMEs  and a venture capital environment that has genuinely improved   What is too slow  Scaling  In Lutz s words   we are good at inventing things and building prototypes  we struggle with scaling   The gap is specific  Companies can raise early money  and once they pass roughly    million Euro in revenue a later stage ecosystem funds them  In between  there is a hole  The European Commission sees it  But the problem is far from being solved  And the real constraint is risk appetite  not cost  Automation has reduced the role of labour costs  What holds us country  built on a strong talent pipeline  Light Conversion grew into the world s most important femtosecond laser maker from that base  Germany is where the next bet sits  Marvel Fusion is now the LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

qubits  and industry reality  focused on scalable products   At the moment  they re not aligned  While the science is forging ahead  the market is lagging in building the next generation hardware needed to protect our critical infrastructure   The timeline is tight  According to some predictions  quantum hardware capable of cracking current security algorithms could exist within three years  Andrew Shields of Toshiba Europe UK thought a ten year horizon was more realistic  but there s great urgency nonetheless  Alongside resilient hardware  we also need new data protocols and to facilitate Quantum Key Distribution from space   a vital step in scaling these networks from regional to global models   For me  the key message was Jose s rallying cry at the end of his opening Alongside the researchers and companies developing the tech  we need to educate the wider community about what quantum will offer   the great benefits  but also the threats to our critical WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

Lumentum  did something rare  he showed us a working prototype and explained exactly how it was built  Watch his presentation here    Matt came to Lumentum after    years at Intel  where he worked on WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica

SABIC GRAND TOUR AND THE CHALLENGE OF REFLOW SOLDERING On our way to Belgium  Optica just visited 沙特基礎工業公司 s Opto Electronic Centre of Excellence in Bergen op Zoom  The Netherlands  We got the full tour with Gabrie Hoogland and Young Joon Choi to understand how new materials can solve one problem that catches optical designers off guard  reflow soldering  The interview is    minutes and is therefore available on YouTube    JEDEC protocols run at     C  three passes  Most thermoplastic resins deform at that temperature  Most optical designers discover this at the packaging stage  not the design stage   沙特基礎工業公司 developed Extem   a thermoplastic polyimide with a glass transition temperature of     C   specifically to close that gap  It survives reflow  can be injection moulded with  nm surface roughness and sub micron dimensional tolerances  and is capable of millions of parts per year  Three things stood out from the visit      Alignment before reflow is now possible  Package your optics on the board first  then solder  That changes the economics for OSAT companies      Epoxy is avoidable  Extem and Ultem can be metallised and self aligned on a PCB via solder paste capillary action  No adhesive required      Detachable connectors work  A demonstrator built with Tyndall National Institute showed     dB penalty over    make and break cycles using expanded beam microlens arrays  The loss came from the PIC design  not the lenses  So  if you are designing for co packaged optics and have not checked your material s reflow compatibility  check now   Interested in more information  Contact Gabrie Hoogland and tell them you saw the Optica interview

NANOIMPRINT LITHOGRAPHY FINDS ITS KILLER APPLICATION  CO PACKAGED OPTICS Two conversations  One in Eindhoven  one at ITF     in Antwerp  Both pointed to the same conclusion  SCIL Nanoimprint Solutions is positioning itself at a critical junction in the co packaged optics supply chain   I spoke with James Quinn  CEO  at High Tech Campus Eindhoven  and with Erik Peters  Chief Commercial Officer  during imec s ITF     in mid May       The  NIL  technology has been around for    years  That is actually the point  Nanoimprint lithography has had two decades to mature   throughput is up  defect rates are down  and inorganic materials that survive reflow soldering at     C are now production ready  What was missing was the application  Co packaged optics is that application   What SCIL brings is not just equipment  It is a combination of process know how  proprietary materials  and an equipment platform   all developed in house  The materials cure at room temperature via a purely chemical process  so there is no thermal distortion  The result  critical dimensions down to    nanometers  parabolic mirrors and lenses with the shape precision needed to hit target focal lengths  and optical patterns that survive the full back end process  including reflow soldering  without shrinkage or degradation   James Quinn put the timing bluntly  the next    to    months will set the supply chain for the next decade  Decisions are being made now  and SCIL is building the infrastructure to be in the room   a direct presence in Taiwan  an application centre planned for Singapore  and business development hiring underway in Silicon Valley  Erik Peters framed the product position clearly  SCIL Nanoimprint Solutions prints optical patterns directly on chip and on plugs to make fiber to chip a pluggable solution  The company is not just shipping equipment  It is running pre production and pilot lines for customers while they qualify their devices   a deliberate strategy to become a design win partner  not a component vendor   The 飛利浦 lineage matters here  SCIL was incubated inside Philips for    to    years before spinning out  James Quinn described it as the second largest lithography spinout from Philips  after 艾司摩爾  That heritage shows in the depth of the materials IP and in the manufacturing discipline the team brings  The vision Quinn sketched   ASML handling HBM stacking  SCIL handling the photonics  both ending up on the same photonic interposer   is not a marketing slide  It reflects where the substrate roadmap is heading  imec xpand is the lead investor  and Erik Peters was direct about the value  not just capital  but connections and technology direction  Being inside the imec ecosystem at a moment when the CPO supply chain is still being assembled is a structural advantage  The honest constraint  SCIL cannot be everywhere at once    #photonics  #nanoimprint  #copackagedoptics  #CPO  #microoptics  #ITF      #semiconductors  #Eindhoven

JAPAN JUST BET     BILLION YEN ON A MATERIAL MOST PEOPLE CANNOT NAME  For years  indium phosphide was the material our community had to explain to everyone else  Now it is the material everyone else is explaining to us   Look at Japan   On    June  JX Advanced Metals Corporation  company video below  committed up to     billion yen over four years to expand InP substrate capacity  The largest investment the company has ever made in this product line  New capacity in Hitachinaka alongside the existing Isohara Works  targeting   to    times current output  Counting the three earlier expansions since July       the total is around     billion yen   Two smaller details tell you more   JX said it is opening discussions with customers about price revisions  Anyone who has bought substrates knows what that means  This has been a thin margin business for a long time  and the supplier has just noticed it is holding the constraint   JX also now calls InP a future revenue pillar alongside its semiconductor sputtering targets  I have watched many companies say photonics is strategic  Committing     billion yen is a different kind of statement   Why now is no mystery  Silicon guides light  modulates it  splits it  It does not generate it  Every    G and    T module  and every co packaged optics architecture behind them  still needs an InP laser as its source  Lumentum s CEO Michael Hurlston said on   August that the InP supply and demand gap now exceeds DRAM and NAND  Orders that used to arrive in the hundreds from telecom customers now arrive in the hundreds of millions of devices   What I find most interesting is that three regions are answering the same question in three different ways   The United States is answering with capital  NVIDIA put   billion dollars each into Coherent Corp  and Lumentum in March  with long term supply agreements attached  Coherent broke ground in Texas in June on a   inch InP fab expansion  backed by a proposed    million dollar US CHIPS Act grant   China is answering with integration  Yunnan Chihong Zinc Germanium Co   Ltd  scaling   inch substrates  San An Optoelectronics Co   Ltd  running substrate to chip in a single house  Remember  China also refines roughly    percent of the world s indium and has tightened export controls since        Japan is answering with depth  JX is not moving downstream into lasers or modules  It is making itself the layer nobody can design around   None of this rescues       Indium comes out of zinc refining as a by product  so the feedstock does not respond to demand signals  Large diameter InP crystal growth takes years of patient yield work  Analysts expect the imbalance to run past       and JX s new capacity arrives late in the decade   So what do we conclude  The bottleneck in AI infrastructure right now is not a transistor problem  It is a crystal growth problem  Photonics is no longer the interesting adjacent field  It is the critical path   Sources THE DEMCON      PHOTONICS GRAND TOUR   THE BIG OPPORTUNITIES Demcon is one of Optica s largest engineering corporate members  and it has recently set up a dedicated photonics division  I spent a day there with the managing director for Demcon photonics  Thijs Kniknie  and it was quite an experience   We discussed a lot in this interview  From their existing collaborations in space and in house manufacturing to the catalytic role they are playing in several regions of the world  including  #Enschede   One highlight for me was a system built under an EU Horizon project for analysing microfluidic samples  designed to detect pathogens in blood and other fluids  Look inside the box and you see how much has to work together  The sample sits on a microfluidic chip that carries a passive photonic element  An active element at the back of the machine aligns to that chip with six degrees of freedom  reads it out using Raman spectroscopy  and processes the data on board before the operator swaps in the next chip  Photonics  mechatronics  microfluidics and medical compliance  all in one enclosure  with DEMCON having developed the complete electronics and mechanics    Then Thijs Kniknie raised something bigger  DEMCON is working on laser writing technologies that can write waveguides in situ and remove the need for active alignment  Everyone in this field understands that active alignment will not carry us to the volumes photonics needs  Solving that is a scaling problem  not a lab problem  So here is the open call  DEMCON wants to talk to two kinds of companies  those with a laser writing process proven at lab scale that needs to become real equipment  and those with the technology and a product to sell who need the machine to make it   If that is you  contact Thijs directly  mentioning this Optica video interview  Who will step forward

WHEN THE DRONE TETHER IS MADE OF GLASS  I listened to a 英國廣播公司 Radio   documentary this week called Britain s Robot Army  One passing detail stopped me  and I think it belongs to our industry rather than to the defence press   The drones reshaping the front line in Ukraine are increasingly guided by a bare optical fibre paying out from a spool bolted to the airframe  No radio link  so nothing to jam  Nobody said who makes that fibre  So we went and found out   Three things worth your attention   It is not a bespoke defence product  It is ITU T G     A  bend insensitive single mode fibre  the same category developed for tight radius routing in fibre to the home       and      nm      micron coating  dynamic bend radius down to about     mm  The property that lets you turn a corner in an apartment block is the property that lets a drone unspool    km at speed without macrobend loss   Fibre guided drones and AI data centres are now bidding for the same product  Chinese cable went from    yuan per kilometre in January      to    yuan in January       according to Vedomosti via the Kyiv Post  Russia and Ukraine together consume an estimated    to    million fibre kilometres a year  The upstream constraint appears to be preform capacity  which nobody expands quickly  A commodity telecom fibre has acquired a second  price inelastic customer base  and our industry did not plan for that   The specialist value has moved from the glass to the spool  Nobody draws fibre for drones  What matters is winding geometry  packing process  tension control and payout mechanics  because failures in flight are mechanical rather than optical  The firms doing that work well are small  European and American  and most of them are not yet part of our community   The full analysis is in the EXPLORING PUBLIC CPO FOUNDRY ROADMAPS  Only four foundries have put a real co packaged optics roadmap in public  TSMC  Intel  Samsung and GlobalFoundries  Tom s Hardware has broken all four down  and it is worth your weekend or holiday catch up having a look   The useful part is that these are not four versions of one plan  They are four business models  and that decides where the rest of us can sell   台積電 is building a closed platform tied to its own packaging  moving the optical engine from the board  to the substrate beside a switch ASIC  to the interposer inside the package at      Tbps    英特爾 is narrower on purpose  an optical chiplet that attaches to compute over PCIe  aimed at CPUs and accelerators  explicitly not at switches    三星電子 has the longest ladder on paper  ending with lasers integrated alongside compute and memory from         GlobalFoundries is the outlier and the one that leaves room for everyone else  selling bespoke  standards compliant optical engines that customers package themselves   Two things I would take from all this   Energy is becoming the unit of account  Samsung s public numbers run from roughly    picojoules per bit today  to    to   at interposer integration  Component roadmaps should be written against that scale   The laser stays outside the package longest  On the most aggressive roadmap published  full integration does not arrive until       Until then lasers  fibre array units  alignment and test remain open  and that is precisely where European suppliers are strong   Full piece below  Credit to Anton Shilov for the reporting  Head over for full details  Link

PROMISED UPDATE  Japanese chip plants restart after Kumamoto earthquake Semiconductor facilities in the Kumamoto area began restarting within days of Tuesday s magnitude     earthquake  Renesas Electronics resumed production at its Nishiki plant on Wednesday night after confirming clean room integrity and expects its Kawashiri plant in Kumamoto city  in operation since       to restart on   August despite wall cracks and water leaks  Tokyo Electron resumed partial operations at Koshi and Ozu from Thursday with full scale production possible from Monday  and president Toshiki Kawai said the earnings impact should be minor  Mitsubishi Electric restarted some power chip production at Kikuchi and Koshi on Thursday afternoon  台積電 and 索尼 had not set timelines for their Kikuyo plants as of Thursday evening  with TSMC citing equipment adjustment work  Toshiya Suzuki of Omdia  OPTICA CORPORATE MEMBER  attributed the speed of recovery to seismic isolation in fab construction and to business continuity planning   What this means  The recovery time is the real story  A decade ago  the same region took roughly three months to restore chip production  this time  most plants are back up and running within a week  and Sony expects pre quake output by mid August  Geographic concentration risk in Kumamoto has not gone away  but the cost of that risk has fallen sharply  which weakens one argument European policymakers have used for onshoring  Suppliers of contamination sensitive optical and metrology equipment should note the specific failure mode reported by TSMC suppliers  impurity accumulation in process equipment that requires cleaning or replacement  rather than structural damage   One more thing  Japan has joined Horizon Europe

witnessing a small team turn silicon nitride photonic integrated circuits into a full RGB light engine  small enough for AR glasses and thin enough for a car dashboard  PICs have lived mainly in datacom and telecom for two decades  Brilliance RGB  founded about three years ago  is pushing the same platform into a market with far higher volume  visible light for AR VR eyewear  automotive AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly       switches  and Axonal s architecture is aimed at cutting that to around      while staying compatible with existing Ethernet  InfiniBand  leaf spine designs so operators wouldn t need to rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in the New Frontiers in Sustainable Computing category     startups were selected for the virtual pitch event coming up this week on July        with       finalists advancing to pitch live at SEMICON West      in San Francisco this October  Congratulations to David and the team

CHINA ADDS POLISH VIGO Photonics TO EXPORT CONTROL LIST in response to EU Russia sanctions  China s Ministry of Commerce announced on    July that it has added    EU entities  including Germany s Rheinmetall and Poland based infrared detector and laser maker VIGO Photonics S A   to its export control list  banning the export of dual use items to them with immediate effect  The ministry framed the move as protecting national security and fulfilling non proliferation obligations  Adam Piotrowski CEO of VIGO Photonics said  in comments carried by Reuters  that being placed on the list would not have a critical impact on its operations   What this means   This is a rare case of a named  publicly listed European photonics company being caught up directly in the EU China sanctions exchange  rather than the larger defence and general semiconductor names that typically populate such lists  Even though Vigo Photonics has played down the operational impact  the listing signals that Beijing is willing to reach into the mid cap photonics and infrared sensing supply chain when retaliating against Brussels  a factor European photonics companies with any China linked supply chain should now weigh in compliance and sourcing planning  That Beijing s response followed the EU s sanctions package by only a day  and matched its scale one for one  is widely read by trade analysts as a deliberate signal rather than a coincidence  However  China s own statement does not frame it that way   Sources  CGTN  Reuters  via TradingView

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

CANADA S PHOTONICS MOMENT  WHY THE CPFC SPINOFF CHANGES EVERYTHING FOR WESTERN SEMICONDUCTOR SUPPLY CHAINS  The Canadian Photonics Fabrication Center is being spun off from the National Research Council Canada   Conseil national de recherches Canada as a private  independent foundry  That is not a minor administrative change  It is the moment a fragmented set of assets becomes a coherent supply chain   I chatted with Paul Slaby  Managing Director of the Canadian Semiconductor Council  to understand what this actually means    for the industry  for AI infrastructure  and for Western supply chain sovereignty   A few things that struck me from this conversation  CPFC is now the only pure play III V foundry in North America  One of very few in the world  And it sits at the center of a cluster most people outside the industry have not yet mapped  Ciena s global R D is managed out of Ottawa  諾基亞 s Optical Division is headquartered there  捷普集團 s co packaged optics R D facility is in Kanata  Inphos  building devices directly from CPFC output  is run by Joe Costello  This is not a collection of companies  It is a supply chain   Paul is direct about what scaling this requires  Current CPFC assets are around half a billion dollars  He puts the investment needed to make this fully competitive    from wafer capacity expansion to the R D required to hit the yields AI applications demand from high power indium phosphide    somewhere between    billion and     billion  Large numbers  But not TSMC scale silicon numbers  And the demand justification is there  the compound semiconductor market is forecast to grow from roughly    billion today to     billion within five years  driven almost entirely by AI data center optical interconnect requirements   We also get into critical minerals  Canada holds the second largest known reserves of the rare earth materials that III V manufacturing depends on  The challenge is not what is in the ground  It is the decade long timeline to bring a mine from discovery to production ready output  That conversation on substrate supply and minerals sovereignty is one of the more frank exchanges in the interview   If you are building partnerships in Canada  evaluating the Ottawa photonics cluster  or trying to understand where Western compound semiconductor capacity is actually coming from    this is    minutes worth your time

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

SABIC GRAND TOUR AND THE CHALLENGE OF REFLOW SOLDERING On our way to Belgium  Optica just visited 沙特基礎工業公司 s Opto Electronic Centre of Excellence in Bergen op Zoom  The Netherlands  We got the full tour with Gabrie Hoogland and Young Joon Choi to understand how new materials can solve one problem that catches optical designers off guard  reflow soldering  The interview is    minutes and is therefore available on YouTube    JEDEC protocols run at     C  three passes  Most thermoplastic resins deform at that temperature  Most optical designers discover this at the packaging stage  not the design stage   沙特基礎工業公司 developed Extem   a thermoplastic polyimide with a glass transition temperature of     C   specifically to close that gap  It survives reflow  can be injection moulded with  nm surface roughness and sub micron dimensional tolerances  and is capable of millions of parts per year  Three things stood out from the visit      Alignment before reflow is now possible  Package your optics on the board first  then solder  That changes the economics for OSAT companies      Epoxy is avoidable  Extem and Ultem can be metallised and self aligned on a PCB via solder paste capillary action  No adhesive required      Detachable connectors work  A demonstrator built with Tyndall National Institute showed     dB penalty over    make and break cycles using expanded beam microlens arrays  The loss came from the PIC design  not the lenses  So  if you are designing for co packaged optics and have not checked your material s reflow compatibility  check now   Interested in more information  Contact Gabrie Hoogland and tell them you saw the Optica interview

Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

some of the earliest heterogeneous integration in client computing  including glass core substrates and early chiplet stacking  He brought that background to a deceptively simple question  how do you package VCSELs with CMOS in a way that s actually manufacturable   His answer was fan out wafer level packaging  FOWLP    a process already running at volume in your smartphone  He dropped III V VCSEL die  photodiodes  a TIA and a driver into a standard OSAT flow  following existing design rules without inventing a single new process step  The result  a compact optic engine      x    mm   roughly deliberate  He wanted to de risk everything downstream   fibre integration  board validation  test   so he kept the assembly flow completely conventional  That discipline is what allowed the team to debut the package at OFC earlier this year   Matt s broader point was equally sharp  the photonics industry doesn t need to repeat the painful early years of advanced semiconductor packaging  The yield learning  the process infrastructure  the OSAT ecosystem   it already exists  The opportunity is to design optical solutions around what works  rather than starting from scratch   On standards WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica

AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

IBM CRASH  IS PHOTONICS OR QUANTUM THE CAUSE OR SOLUTION  On Tuesday July   th  IBM had its worst trading day in     years  Shares fell     after the company warned that Q  results would miss expectations  roughly      B in revenue and       adjusted EPS against a       consensus  ahead of the full report on July      The short answer to the headline  neither  And that is the interesting part  The cause was an AI budget war  In the final weeks of June  enterprise customers redirected capex toward supply constrained AI infrastructure  meaning servers  storage  and memory  ahead of expected price increases driven by rising chip and memory costs  That squeezed the budgets IBM lives on  software grew only    against a double digit target  consulting was flat  and infrastructure fell    on weak mainframe sales  CEO Arvind Krishna was blunt   We did not adapt and move quickly enough   Quantum is not the cause  One day after the crash  IBM reaffirmed its    B  five year quantum investment  still targeting a fault tolerant machine by       Could photonics be part of the solution  Follow the money  The capex that abandoned IBM s software this quarter went into AI datacenter hardware  and that is precisely where optical interconnects and co packaged optics are becoming the bottleneck technology  The spending wave that hurt IBM s quarter is the same one pulling photonics into the datacenter   One bad quarter is not a verdict on IBM s deep tech roadmap  But it is an early  expensive data point on where enterprise money is actually going in       And if you have not watched it  remember the excellent keynote from Bert Jan Offrein at GAMA          Other Sources

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

CANADA S PHOTONICS MOMENT  WHY THE CPFC SPINOFF CHANGES EVERYTHING FOR WESTERN SEMICONDUCTOR SUPPLY CHAINS  The Canadian Photonics Fabrication Center is being spun off from the National Research Council Canada   Conseil national de recherches Canada as a private  independent foundry  That is not a minor administrative change  It is the moment a fragmented set of assets becomes a coherent supply chain   I chatted with Paul Slaby  Managing Director of the Canadian Semiconductor Council  to understand what this actually means    for the industry  for AI infrastructure  and for Western supply chain sovereignty   A few things that struck me from this conversation  CPFC is now the only pure play III V foundry in North America  One of very few in the world  And it sits at the center of a cluster most people outside the industry have not yet mapped  Ciena s global R D is managed out of Ottawa  諾基亞 s Optical Division is headquartered there  捷普集團 s co packaged optics R D facility is in Kanata  Inphos  building devices directly from CPFC output  is run by Joe Costello  This is not a collection of companies  It is a supply chain   Paul is direct about what scaling this requires  Current CPFC assets are around half a billion dollars  He puts the investment needed to make this fully competitive    from wafer capacity expansion to the R D required to hit the yields AI applications demand from high power indium phosphide    somewhere between    billion and     billion  Large numbers  But not TSMC scale silicon numbers  And the demand justification is there  the compound semiconductor market is forecast to grow from roughly    billion today to     billion within five years  driven almost entirely by AI data center optical interconnect requirements   We also get into critical minerals  Canada holds the second largest known reserves of the rare earth materials that III V manufacturing depends on  The challenge is not what is in the ground  It is the decade long timeline to bring a mine from discovery to production ready output  That conversation on substrate supply and minerals sovereignty is one of the more frank exchanges in the interview   If you are building partnerships in Canada  evaluating the Ottawa photonics cluster  or trying to understand where Western compound semiconductor capacity is actually coming from    this is    minutes worth your time

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon
Excellent summary  Worth your time reading

LEARN FROM Lumentum  BORROWED FROM SEMICONDUCTORS  BUILT FOR PHOTONICS  THE PACKAGING MOVE AI CONNECTIVITY NEEDS At Optica GAMA last week  June            Matt Guzy  Advanced Packaging lead at Lumentum  did something rare  he showed us a working prototype and explained exactly how it was built  Watch his presentation here    Matt came to Lumentum after    years at Intel  where he worked on some of the earliest heterogeneous integration in client computing  including glass core substrates and early chiplet stacking  He brought that background to a deceptively simple question  how do you package VCSELs with CMOS in a way that s actually manufacturable   His answer was fan out wafer level packaging  FOWLP    a process already running at volume in your smartphone  He dropped III V VCSEL die  photodiodes  a TIA and a driver into a standard OSAT flow  following existing design rules without inventing a single new process step  The result  a compact optic engine      x    mm   roughly the size of a tic tac   capable of      Tb s across    channels at    Gbps per channel  at under     pJ bit  with bandwidth density above     Tb s per millimeter   The engineering choices were deliberate  He wanted to de risk everything downstream   fibre integration  board validation  test   so he kept the assembly flow completely conventional  That discipline is what allowed the team to debut the package at OFC earlier this year   Matt s broader point was equally sharp  the photonics industry doesn t need to repeat the painful early years of advanced semiconductor packaging  The yield learning  the process infrastructure  the OSAT ecosystem   it already exists  The opportunity is to design optical solutions around what works  rather than starting from scratch   On standards  he was pragmatic  wait    to    months  The field is too fragmented today to standardise usefully  When two or three approaches pull ahead  standards will follow naturally and will actually mean something   On the VCSEL vs  external laser question  he was clear eyed  VCSELs are not a universal answer  They don t have the reach for scale across applications  But for within rack and rack to rack  they offer a lower cost  lower power  high bandwidth option that doesn t require reinventing the supply chain   The photonics community tends to treat packaging as a downstream problem  Matt s work suggests it should be the starting point

WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica
