SABIC GRAND TOUR AND THE CHALLENGE OF REFLOW SOLDERING On our way to Belgium  Optica just visited 沙特基礎工業公司 s Opto Electronic Centre of Excellence in Bergen op Zoom  The Netherlands  We got the full tour with Gabrie Hoogland and Young Joon Choi to understand how new materials can solve one problem that catches optical designers off guard  reflow soldering  The interview is    minutes and is therefore available on YouTube    JEDEC protocols run at     C  three passes  Most thermoplastic resins deform at that temperature  Most optical designers discover this at the packaging stage  not the design stage   沙特基礎工業公司 developed Extem   a thermoplastic polyimide with a glass transition temperature of     C   specifically to close that gap  It survives reflow  can be injection moulded with  nm surface roughness and sub micron dimensional tolerances  and is capable of millions of parts per year  Three things stood out from the visit      Alignment before reflow is now possible  Package your optics on the board first  then solder  That changes the economics for OSAT companies      Epoxy is avoidable  Extem and Ultem can be metallised and self aligned on a PCB via solder paste capillary action  No adhesive required      Detachable connectors work  A demonstrator built with Tyndall National Institute showed     dB penalty over    make and break cycles using expanded beam microlens arrays  The loss came from the PIC design  not the lenses  So  if you are designing for co packaged optics and have not checked your material s reflow compatibility  check now   Interested in more information  Contact Gabrie Hoogland and tell them you saw the Optica interview

than to the defence press   The drones reshaping the front line in Ukraine are increasingly guided by a bare optical fibre paying out from a spool bolted to the airframe  No radio link  so nothing to jam  Nobody said who makes that fibre  So we went and found out   Three things worth your attention   It is not a bespoke defence product  It is ITU T G     A  bend insensitive single mode fibre  the same category developed for tight radius routing in fibre to the home       and      nm      micron coating  dynamic bend radius down to about     mm  The property that lets you turn a corner in an apartment block is the property that lets a drone unspool    km at speed without macrobend loss   Fibre guided drones and AI data centres are now bidding for the same product  Chinese cable went from    yuan per kilometre in January      to    yuan in January       according to Vedomosti via the Kyiv Post  Russia and Ukraine together consume an estimated    to    million fibre kilometres a year  The upstream constraint appears to be preform capacity  which nobody expands quickly  A commodity telecom fibre has acquired a second  price inelastic customer base  and our industry did not plan for that   The specialist value has moved from the glass to the spool  Nobody draws fibre for drones  What matters is winding geometry  packing process  tension control and payout mechanics  because failures in flight are mechanical rather than optical  The firms doing that work well are small  European and American  and most of them are not yet part of our community   The full analysis is in the AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly       switches  and Axonal s architecture is aimed at cutting that to around      while staying compatible with existing Ethernet  InfiniBand  leaf spine designs so operators wouldn t need to rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in the New Frontiers in Sustainable Computing category     startups were selected for the virtual pitch event coming up this week on July        with       finalists advancing to pitch live at SEMICON West      in San Francisco this October  Congratulations to David and the team

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

IBM CRASH  IS PHOTONICS OR QUANTUM THE CAUSE OR SOLUTION  On Tuesday July   th  IBM had its worst trading day in     years  Shares fell     after the company warned that Q  results would miss expectations  roughly      B in revenue and       adjusted EPS against a       consensus  ahead of the full report on July      The short answer to the headline  neither  And that is the interesting part  The cause was an AI budget war  In the final weeks of June  enterprise customers redirected capex toward supply constrained AI infrastructure  meaning servers  storage  and memory  ahead of expected price increases driven by rising chip and memory costs  That squeezed the budgets IBM lives on  software grew only    against a double digit target  consulting was flat  and infrastructure fell    on weak mainframe sales  CEO Arvind Krishna was blunt   We did not adapt and move quickly enough   Quantum is not the cause  One day after the crash  IBM reaffirmed its    B  five year quantum investment  still targeting a fault tolerant machine by       Could photonics be part of the solution  Follow the money  The capex that abandoned IBM s software this quarter went into AI datacenter hardware  and that is precisely where optical interconnects and co packaged optics are becoming the bottleneck technology  The spending wave that hurt IBM s quarter is the same one pulling photonics into the datacenter   One bad quarter is not a verdict on IBM s deep tech roadmap  But it is an early  expensive data point on where enterprise money is actually going in       And if you have not watched it  remember the excellent keynote from Bert Jan Offrein at GAMA          Other Sources

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

Lumentum  did something rare  he showed us a working prototype and explained exactly how it was built  Watch his presentation here    Matt came to Lumentum after    years at Intel  where he worked on some of the earliest heterogeneous integration in client computing  including glass core substrates and early chiplet stacking  He brought that background to a deceptively simple question  how do you package VCSELs with CMOS in a way that s actually manufacturable   His answer was fan out wafer level packaging  FOWLP    a process already running at volume in your smartphone  He dropped III V VCSEL die  photodiodes  a TIA and a driver into a standard OSAT flow  following existing design rules without inventing a single new process step  The result  a compact optic engine      x    mm   roughly the size of a tic tac   capable of      Tb s across    channels at    Gbps per channel  at under     pJ bit  with bandwidth density above     Tb s per millimeter   The engineering choices were deliberate  He wanted to de risk everything downstream   fibre integration  board validation  test   so he kept the assembly flow completely conventional  That discipline is what allowed the team to debut the package at OFC earlier this year   Matt s broader point was equally sharp  the photonics industry doesn t need to repeat the painful early years of advanced semiconductor packaging  The yield learning  the process infrastructure  the OSAT ecosystem   it already exists  The opportunity is to design optical solutions around what works  rather than starting from scratch   On standards WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica

AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly       switches  and Axonal s architecture is aimed at cutting that to around      while staying compatible with existing Ethernet  InfiniBand  leaf spine designs so operators wouldn t need to rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in the New Frontiers in Sustainable Computing category     startups were selected for the virtual pitch event coming up this week on July        with       finalists advancing to pitch live at SEMICON West      in San Francisco this October  Congratulations to David and the team

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

IBM CRASH  IS PHOTONICS OR QUANTUM THE CAUSE OR SOLUTION  On Tuesday July   th  IBM had its worst trading day in     years  Shares fell     after the company warned that Q  results would miss expectations  roughly      B in revenue and       adjusted EPS against a       consensus  ahead of the full report on July      The short answer to the headline  neither  And that is the interesting part  The cause was an AI budget war  In the final weeks of June  enterprise customers redirected capex toward supply constrained AI infrastructure  meaning servers  storage  and memory  ahead of expected price increases driven by rising chip and memory costs  That squeezed the budgets IBM lives on  software grew only    against a double digit target  consulting was flat  and infrastructure fell    on weak mainframe sales  CEO Arvind Krishna was blunt   We did not adapt and move quickly enough   Quantum is not the cause  One day after the crash  IBM reaffirmed its    B  five year quantum investment  still targeting a fault tolerant machine by       Could photonics be part of the solution  Follow the money  The capex that abandoned IBM s software this quarter went into AI datacenter hardware  and that is precisely where optical interconnects and co packaged optics are becoming the bottleneck technology  The spending wave that hurt IBM s quarter is the same one pulling photonics into the datacenter   One bad quarter is not a verdict on IBM s deep tech roadmap  But it is an early  expensive data point on where enterprise money is actually going in       And if you have not watched it  remember the excellent keynote from Bert Jan Offrein at GAMA          Other Sources

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

LEARN FROM Lumentum  BORROWED FROM SEMICONDUCTORS  BUILT FOR PHOTONICS  THE PACKAGING MOVE AI CONNECTIVITY NEEDS At Optica GAMA last week  June            Matt Guzy  Advanced Packaging lead at Lumentum  did something rare  he showed us a working prototype and explained exactly how it was built  Watch his presentation here    Matt came to Lumentum after    years at Intel  where he worked on some of the earliest heterogeneous integration in client computing  including glass core substrates and early chiplet stacking  He brought that background to a deceptively simple question  how do you package VCSELs with CMOS in a way that s actually manufacturable   His answer was fan out wafer level packaging  FOWLP    a process already running at volume in your smartphone  He dropped III V VCSEL die  photodiodes  a TIA and a driver into a standard OSAT flow  following existing design rules without inventing a single new process step  The result  a compact optic engine      x    mm   roughly the size of a tic tac   capable of      Tb s across    channels at    Gbps per channel  at under     pJ bit  with bandwidth density above     Tb s per millimeter   The engineering choices were deliberate  He wanted to de risk everything downstream   fibre integration  board validation  test   so he kept the assembly flow completely conventional  That discipline is what allowed the team to debut the package at OFC earlier this year   Matt s broader point was equally sharp  the photonics industry doesn t need to repeat the painful early years of advanced semiconductor packaging  The yield learning  the process infrastructure  the OSAT ecosystem   it already exists  The opportunity is to design optical solutions around what works  rather than starting from scratch   On standards  he was pragmatic  wait    to    months  The field is too fragmented today to standardise usefully  When two or three approaches pull ahead  standards will follow naturally and will actually mean something   On the VCSEL vs  external laser question  he was clear eyed  VCSELs are not a universal answer  They don t have the reach for scale across applications  But for within rack and rack to rack  they offer a lower cost  lower power  high bandwidth option that doesn t require reinventing the supply chain   The photonics community tends to treat packaging as a downstream problem  Matt s work suggests it should be the starting point

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A    POUND INSTRUMENT FITS ON A CHIP At the GAMA meeting in Brussels on June  rd  Diana Mojahed  PhD  CEO of Optica Corporate member Lightfinder  based in Boston USA   closed the conference with something the room had not seen before  Lightfinder has built a chip based optical spectrum analyzer on standard silicon photonics  No exotic materials  No moving parts  A device that fits in a small enclosure    and delivers spectral resolution and bandwidth comparable to a Yokogawa OSA that weighs    pounds and costs tens of thousands of dollars per unit  The technology is a digital Fourier transform spectrometer  a cascade of Mach Zehnder interferometers on a silicon photonic chip  using a single photodetector and a Fourier domain encoding scheme to achieve very competitive resolution  Add one stage to the architecture  and you double your channel count    an exponential scaling property that conventional dispersive spectrometers simply cannot match   Why does this matter for our industry  Because co packaged optics is heading toward volume production  and optical testing has not kept up  ATE companies can run        electronic tests simultaneously for semiconductor process control  medical diagnostics  remote sensing  and industrial inspection  The same silicon photonic infrastructure being built for datacenters could produce sensing chips at a volume that rivals CPO itself  If you are working in photonic packaging  test  or sensing    and you are not already talking to LightFinder    now is the time  Diana Mojahed can be reached at diana WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica

SABIC GRAND TOUR AND THE CHALLENGE OF REFLOW SOLDERING On our way to Belgium  Optica just visited 沙特基礎工業公司 s Opto Electronic Centre of Excellence in Bergen op Zoom  The Netherlands  We got the full tour with Gabrie Hoogland and Young Joon Choi to understand how new materials can solve one problem that catches optical designers off guard  reflow soldering  The interview is    minutes and is therefore available on YouTube    JEDEC protocols run at     C  three passes  Most thermoplastic resins deform at that temperature  Most optical designers discover this at the packaging stage  not the design stage   沙特基礎工業公司 developed Extem   a thermoplastic polyimide with a glass transition temperature of     C   specifically to close that gap  It survives reflow  can be injection moulded with  nm surface roughness and sub micron dimensional tolerances  and is capable of millions of parts per year  Three things stood out from the visit      Alignment before reflow is now possible  Package your optics on the board first  then solder  That changes the economics for OSAT companies      Epoxy is avoidable  Extem and Ultem can be metallised and self aligned on a PCB via solder paste capillary action  No adhesive required      Detachable connectors work  A demonstrator built with Tyndall National Institute showed     dB penalty over    make and break cycles using expanded beam microlens arrays  The loss came from the PIC design  not the lenses  So  if you are designing for co packaged optics and have not checked your material s reflow compatibility  check now   Interested in more information  Contact Gabrie Hoogland and tell them you saw the Optica interview

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

companies up there  each holding one piece of a puzzle nobody has solved yet  how do you get co packaged optics into data centers in two years  not five   Coherent Corp  brought socket CPO  POET Technologies argued for putting the laser outside the package  easier thermal management  a path to pluggables  Photon Bridge argued for putting it inside  better manufacturability and cost  but harder engineering  The audience in the room was split roughly down the middle  Nobody  including the panelists  had the full answer   Nine months on  with ECOC Exhibition and the Optica Global Photonics Economic Forum both landing in Malaga the same week this September  it s worth checking the scoreboard   Coherent Corp   In March  Nvidia took a    billion equity stake in Coherent and signed a multi year  multi billion dollar purchase commitment covering CPO and optical circuit switching  Coherent used the moment to raise its CPO addressable market estimate to     billion  That is a hyperscaler underwriting the socket CPO bet with capital  not just intent    POET Technologies  At OFC in March  POET showed Blazar  its hybrid laser for CPO and chip to chip optical links  alongside Starlight  a next gen external light source engine  It also has a joint development agreement with Lumilens that includes a     million initial purchase order  and a partnership with Sivers Semiconductors targeting customer prototypes in the first half of      and production readiness by year end    Photon Bridge  Since unveiling its integrated tunable laser PIC last October  it has CANADA S PHOTONICS MOMENT  WHY THE CPFC SPINOFF CHANGES EVERYTHING FOR WESTERN SEMICONDUCTOR SUPPLY CHAINS  The Canadian Photonics Fabrication Center is being spun off from the National Research Council Canada   Conseil national de recherches Canada as a private  independent foundry  That is not a minor administrative change  It is the moment a fragmented set of assets becomes a coherent supply chain   I chatted with Paul Slaby  Managing Director of the Canadian Semiconductor Council  to understand what this actually means    for the industry  for AI infrastructure  and for Western supply chain sovereignty   A few things that struck me from this conversation  CPFC is now the only pure play III V foundry in North America  One of very few in the world  And it sits at the center of a cluster most people outside the industry have not yet mapped  Ciena s global R D is managed out of Ottawa  諾基亞 s Optical Division is headquartered there  捷普集團 s co packaged optics R D facility is in Kanata  Inphos  building devices directly from CPFC output  is run by Joe Costello  This is not a collection of companies  It is a supply chain   Paul is direct about what scaling this requires  Current CPFC assets are around half a billion dollars  He puts the investment needed to make this fully competitive    from wafer capacity expansion to the R D required to hit the yields AI applications demand from high power indium phosphide    somewhere between    billion and     billion  Large numbers  But not TSMC scale silicon numbers  And the demand justification is there  the compound semiconductor market is forecast to grow from roughly    billion today to     billion within five years  driven almost entirely by AI data center optical interconnect requirements   We also get into critical minerals  Canada holds the second largest known reserves of the rare earth materials that III V manufacturing depends on  The challenge is not what is in the ground  It is the decade long timeline to bring a mine from discovery to production ready output  That conversation on substrate supply and minerals sovereignty is one of the more frank exchanges in the interview   If you are building partnerships in Canada  evaluating the Ottawa photonics cluster  or trying to understand where Western compound semiconductor capacity is actually coming from    this is    minutes worth your time

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon
Excellent summary  Worth your time reading

Greater Glasgow was recently ranked the fifth most important quantum cluster in the world  and first globally for its role as a sector hub  That s an incredible achievement for the UK  and a massive nod to Scotland s deep tech ecosystem   This week I ve been following discussions at Optica s Quantum     Conference in Glasgow        June  where one of the themes has been the race to translate raw R D into practical  commercial applications   Jose Pozo  CTO of Optica  captured the challenge  He pointed out that quantum is currently moving at two separate speeds  academic research  measured in qubits  and industry reality  focused on scalable products   At the moment  they re not aligned  While the science is forging ahead  the market is lagging in building the next generation hardware needed to protect our critical infrastructure   The timeline is tight  According to some predictions  quantum hardware capable of cracking current security algorithms could exist within three years  Andrew Shields of Toshiba Europe UK thought a ten year horizon was more realistic  but there s great urgency nonetheless  Alongside resilient hardware  we also need new data protocols and certification standards   It was very positive to hear about the local expertise that s helping to address this challenge  Scottish space company Craft Prospect is already working on using satellites to facilitate Quantum Key Distribution from space   a vital step in scaling these networks from regional to global models   For me  the key message was Jose s rallying cry at the end of his opening presentation   Connect the bench to the market   His advice for closing the divide was direct      To the researchers  Bring the hard problems and the honest data   not the press release    To industry  Bring the real world use cases  the capital  and the procurement appetite to make deployment a reality   In a sector changing this quickly  clear communication is going to play a key role  Alongside the researchers and companies developing the tech  we need to educate the wider community about what quantum will offer   the great benefits  but also the threats to our critical infrastructure and daily lives if research and industry don t align   This ties in perfectly with the work being done by QURECA  which was recently highlighted at the Quantum ARC event in Glasgow  That marked the launch of a new report titled  Inside Scotland s Quantum Ecosystem    yet another reminder of the country s key role in the quantum race

community of       members  mostly SMEs  and a venture capital environment that has genuinely improved   What is too slow  Scaling  In Lutz s words   we are good at inventing things and building  solves the CTE mismatch problem that increasingly limits organic substrates at large panel sizes  and opens a path to integrating  D waveguides directly into the substrate for in package optical LEARN FROM Lumentum  BORROWED FROM SEMICONDUCTORS  BUILT FOR PHOTONICS  THE PACKAGING MOVE AI CONNECTIVITY NEEDS At Optica GAMA last week  June            Matt Guzy  Advanced Packaging lead at Lumentum  did something rare  he showed us a working prototype and explained exactly how it was built  Watch his presentation here    Matt came to Lumentum after    years at Intel  where he worked on some of the earliest heterogeneous integration in client computing  including glass core substrates and early chiplet stacking  He brought that background to a deceptively simple question  how do you package VCSELs with CMOS in a way that s actually manufacturable   His answer was fan out wafer level packaging  FOWLP    a process already running at volume in your smartphone  He dropped III V VCSEL die  photodiodes  a TIA and a driver into a standard OSAT flow  following existing design rules without inventing a single new process step  The result  a compact optic engine      x    mm   roughly the size of a tic tac   capable of      Tb s across    channels at    Gbps per channel  at under     pJ bit  with bandwidth density above     Tb s per millimeter   The engineering choices were deliberate  He wanted to de risk everything downstream   fibre integration  board validation  test   so he kept the assembly flow completely conventional  That discipline is what allowed the team to debut the package at OFC earlier this year   Matt s broader point was equally sharp  the photonics industry doesn t need to repeat the painful early years of advanced semiconductor packaging  The yield learning  the process infrastructure  the OSAT ecosystem   it already exists  The opportunity is to design optical solutions around what works  rather than starting from scratch   On standards  he was pragmatic  wait    to    months  The field is too fragmented today to standardise usefully  When two or three approaches pull ahead  standards will follow naturally and will actually mean something   On the VCSEL vs  external laser question  he was clear eyed  VCSELs are not a universal answer  They don t have the reach for scale across applications  But for within rack and rack to rack  they offer a lower cost  lower power  high bandwidth option that doesn t require reinventing the supply chain   The photonics community tends to treat packaging as a downstream problem  Matt s work suggests it should be the starting point

WHY CO PACKAGED OPTICS FAILED IN        AND WHY IT WON T THIS TIME  At the Optica GAMA Meeting last week  June            Bert Jan Offrein of IBM Research Zurich opened with a question that cuts to the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency  DARPA  funded project is targeting  D optical routing with   micron waveguide pitch  vertical vias  and chip to chip optical bonding through substrates   essentially replicating in the optical domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to system integrator  may matter as much as the technology itself   Bert Jan Offrein presented at the Optica GAMA Meeting  June          Optica brings together the photonics community to accelerate exactly these kinds of industry critical conversations  Why not join us    #Photonics  #CoPackagedOptics  #AIInfrastructure  #Optica

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A    POUND INSTRUMENT FITS ON A CHIP At the GAMA meeting in Brussels on June  rd  Diana Mojahed  PhD  CEO of Optica Corporate member Lightfinder  based in Boston USA   closed the conference with something the room had not seen before  Lightfinder has built a chip based optical spectrum analyzer on standard silicon photonics  No exotic materials  No moving parts  A device that fits in a small enclosure    and delivers spectral resolution and bandwidth comparable to a Yokogawa OSA that weighs    pounds and costs tens of thousands of dollars per unit  The technology is a digital Fourier transform spectrometer  a cascade of Mach Zehnder interferometers on a silicon photonic chip  using a single photodetector and a Fourier domain encoding scheme to achieve very competitive resolution  Add one stage to the architecture  and you double your channel count    an exponential scaling property that conventional dispersive spectrometers simply cannot match   Why The optical test is still stuck at one bench instrument per measurement point  LightFinder is building the chip that changes that ratio   The Optica GAMA audience saw the potential immediately  By the end of the Q A  there were several offers of a packaging and automation partnership from the floor  Beyond CPO  the platform roadmap covers extended NIR and visible wavelengths spectroscopy on a chip for semiconductor process control  medical diagnostics  remote sensing  and industrial inspection  The same silicon photonic infrastructure being built for datacenters could produce sensing chips at a volume that rivals CPO itself  If you are working in photonic packaging  test  or sensing    and you are not already talking to LightFinder    now is the time  Diana Mojahed can be reached at diana SABIC GRAND TOUR AND THE CHALLENGE OF REFLOW SOLDERING On our way to Belgium  Optica just visited 沙特基礎工業公司 s Opto Electronic Centre of Excellence in Bergen op Zoom  The Netherlands  We got the full tour with Gabrie Hoogland and Young Joon Choi to understand how new materials can solve one problem that catches optical designers off guard  reflow soldering  The interview is    minutes and is therefore available on YouTube    JEDEC protocols run at     C  three passes  Most thermoplastic resins deform at that temperature  Most optical designers discover this at the packaging stage  not the design stage   沙特基礎工業公司 developed Extem   a thermoplastic polyimide with a glass transition temperature of     C   specifically to close that gap  It survives reflow  can be injection moulded with  nm surface roughness and sub micron dimensional tolerances  and is capable of millions of parts per year  Three things stood out from the visit      Alignment before reflow is now possible  Package your optics on the board first  then solder  That changes the economics for OSAT companies      Epoxy is avoidable  Extem and Ultem can be metallised and self aligned on a PCB via solder paste capillary action  No adhesive required      Detachable connectors work  A demonstrator built with Tyndall National Institute showed     dB penalty over    make and break cycles using expanded beam microlens arrays  The loss came from the PIC design  not the lenses  So  if you are designing for co packaged optics and have not checked your material s reflow compatibility  check now   Interested in more information  Contact Gabrie Hoogland and tell them you saw the Optica interview

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon
Excellent summary  Worth your time reading

needed to protect our critical infrastructure   The timeline is tight  According to some predictions  quantum hardware capable of cracking current security algorithms could exist within three years certification standards   It was very positive to hear about the local expertise that s helping to address this challenge  Scottish space company Craft Prospect is already working on using satellites to facilitate Quantum Key Distribution from space   a vital step in scaling these networks from regional to global models   For me  the key message was Jose s rallying cry at the end of his opening the heart of where photonics stands today  why  after IBM deployed co packaged optics in a supercomputer back in       did the industry walk away from it for a decade  The answer matters because we re back at the same junction  Follow the link below to watch the    minute presentation on the Optica YouTube channel    In       optics lost to a workaround  The ratio of communication to compute dropped from roughly one byte per flop to less than one hundredth  Electrical systems adapted  and the assembly overhead of optics   the lasers  modulators  drivers  alignment tolerances  fiber routing   simply wasn t worth it   That trade off no longer works  AI training and inference have reversed the pressure  We re back to multi chip modules  back to bandwidth walls  and back to optics as the only credible path forward  But the overhead problem hasn t gone away   Bert s argument is that solving it requires rethinking assembly  not just components  IBM s polymer waveguide approach   where light transitions adiabatically from a silicon or silicon nitride chip waveguide into a polymer matched to fiber mode size   enables     optical connections in a single flip chip attach  That s the direction  optical connectivity that integrates into standard electrical assembly flows  is solder reflow compatible  and is Telcordia tested   Further out  a Defense Advanced Research Projects domain what the back end of line does electrically    Current mirror losses are around   dB and improving  The practical implication  the technology choices that will define the next generation of AI infrastructure won t be decided by peak performance specs  They ll be decided by who solves the assembly overhead at system level   not just the first level package  but across the full board and chassis   IBM Research is now operating as a collaborator rather than a licensor   open to partnerships that can bring these approaches to production  That shift in posture  from IP generator to Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon
Excellent summary  Worth your time reading

qubits  and industry reality  focused on scalable products   At the moment  they re not aligned  While the science is forging ahead  the market is lagging in building the next generation hardware needed to protect our critical infrastructure   The timeline is tight  According to some predictions  quantum hardware capable of cracking current security algorithms could exist within three years  Andrew Shields of Toshiba Europe UK thought a ten year horizon was more realistic  but there s great urgency nonetheless  Alongside resilient hardware  we also need new data protocols and AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in
