AI IS HITTING A WALL  Axonal Networks THINKS PHOTONS CAN FIX IT  I sat down with David Rolston  Founder and CEO of Axonal Networks  at his HQ and labs in Montreal  Rolston previously built Reflex Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to keep ones and zeros intact  Rolston s answer is Digital Photonics  doing the actual switching logic in silicon photonics rather than electronics   The building block is a micro ring modulator  used to construct optical NAND and NOR gates  Micro rings are highly sensitive to temperature and process variation  so Axonal built a thermal feedback stabilization circuit  a small transistor based auto calibrating loop  to keep the rings locked to the laser input   Three products come out of this  paraNu  a high channel count optical transceiver  scaling from   to    channels  paraLITE  optical logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly       switches  and Axonal s architecture is aimed at cutting that to around      while staying compatible with existing Ethernet  InfiniBand  leaf spine designs so operators wouldn t need to rearchitect around it   On manufacturing  Axonal isn t building its own fab  Rolston is leaning on Montreal s photonics ecosystem  four area universities  hubs like C MI and INO  and contract manufacturers including 天弘 and 新美亞 for packaging at production scale   In other news  Axonal Networks has been named a semifinalist in SEMI s Startups for Sustainable Semiconductors  S   program  in the New Frontiers in Sustainable Computing category     startups were selected for the virtual pitch event coming up this week on July        with       finalists advancing to pitch live at SEMICON LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

Photonics before founding Axonal in      with a different starting point  Instead of designing a device and working up  he started with the architecture  then built the devices to match it  The core problem  today s AI switch fabrics move data as electrons through copper  and at scale that means huge power draw  crosstalk  and signal degradation that require heavy correction circuitry just to logic gates for small digital controllers  comparators  and PRBS generators paraDOX  the long term goal  a parallel digital optical cross connect switch fabric targeting thousands of ports  keeping electron movement confined to within a micron inside each logic gate to eliminate EMI and crosstalk  The scale argument is the headline number  Rolston says a         GPU cluster today needs roughly LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

IBM CRASH  IS PHOTONICS OR QUANTUM THE CAUSE OR SOLUTION  On Tuesday July   th  IBM had its worst trading day in     years  Shares fell     after the company warned that Q  results would miss expectations  roughly      B in revenue and       adjusted EPS against a       consensus  ahead of the full report on July      The short answer to the headline  neither  And that is the interesting part  The cause was an AI budget war  In the final weeks of June  enterprise customers redirected capex toward supply constrained AI infrastructure  meaning servers  storage  and memory  ahead of expected price increases driven by rising chip and memory costs  That squeezed the budgets IBM lives on  software grew only    against a double digit target  consulting was flat  and infrastructure fell    on weak mainframe sales  CEO Arvind Krishna was blunt   We did not adapt and move quickly enough   Quantum is not the cause  One day after the crash  IBM reaffirmed its    B  five year quantum investment  still targeting a fault tolerant machine by       Could photonics be part of the solution  Follow the money  The capex that abandoned IBM s software this quarter went into AI datacenter hardware  and that is precisely where optical interconnects and co packaged optics are becoming the bottleneck technology  The spending wave that hurt IBM s quarter is the same one pulling photonics into the datacenter   One bad quarter is not a verdict on IBM s deep tech roadmap  But it is an early  expensive data point on where enterprise money is actually going in       And if you have not watched it  remember the excellent keynote from Bert Jan Offrein at GAMA          Other Sources

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

CANADA S PHOTONICS MOMENT  WHY THE CPFC SPINOFF CHANGES EVERYTHING FOR WESTERN SEMICONDUCTOR SUPPLY CHAINS  The Canadian Photonics Fabrication Center is being spun off from the National Research Council Canada   Conseil national de recherches Canada as a private  independent foundry  That is not a minor administrative change  It is the moment a fragmented set of assets becomes a coherent supply chain   I chatted with Paul Slaby  Managing Director of the Canadian Semiconductor Council  to understand what this actually means    for the industry  for AI infrastructure  and for Western supply chain sovereignty   A few things that struck me from this conversation  CPFC is now the only pure play III V foundry in North America  One of very few in the world  And it sits at the center of a cluster most people outside the industry have not yet mapped  Ciena s global R D is managed out of Ottawa  諾基亞 s Optical Division is headquartered there  捷普集團 s co packaged optics R D facility is in Kanata  Inphos  building devices directly from CPFC output  is run by Joe Costello  This is not a collection of companies  It is a supply chain   Paul is direct about what scaling this requires  Current CPFC assets are around half a billion dollars  He puts the investment needed to make this fully competitive    from wafer capacity expansion to the R D required to hit the yields AI applications demand from high power indium phosphide    somewhere between    billion and     billion  Large numbers  But not TSMC scale silicon numbers  And the demand justification is there  the compound semiconductor market is forecast to grow from roughly    billion today to     billion within five years  driven almost entirely by AI data center optical interconnect requirements   We also get into critical minerals  Canada holds the second largest known reserves of the rare earth materials that III V manufacturing depends on  The challenge is not what is in the ground  It is the decade long timeline to bring a mine from discovery to production ready output  That conversation on substrate supply and minerals sovereignty is one of the more frank exchanges in the interview   If you are building partnerships in Canada  evaluating the Ottawa photonics cluster  or trying to understand where Western compound semiconductor capacity is actually coming from    this is    minutes worth your time

WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon

LASERS ARE THE QUIET HEART OF THE Einstein Telescope Last week I sat down with Stefan Hild  Project Director of ET Pathfinder  at the test facility in  #Maastricht  What I saw changed how I think about the next generation of gravitational wave detectors  and about the role industry plays in getting one built   ET Pathfinder exists to prove out the technology for the Einstein Telescope  the successor to LIGO and Virgo  The ambition  measure the distance between two test masses    meters apart to a precision of       meters  Stefan s comparison stuck with me  It is the equivalent of dropping a single drop of water into the Mediterranean and detecting the rise in sea level  Getting there takes two things working in tandem  The test masses have to be kept extremely still  through vacuum systems and seismic isolation  Then a laser has to detect whether they move at all  and that is where the real difficulty sits  The laser needs a stable reference  here  a    meter cavity with silicon mirrors cooled to cryogenic temperatures to cut thermal noise  Even the cooling has to be engineered around the laser  Sorption coolers with no moving parts are used instead of mechanical compressors  so the act of cooling doesn t introduce the vibration you re trying to eliminate  Beyond that  quantum effects start to matter  Squeezed light and quantum non demolition techniques are being tested to work around the limits set by Heisenberg s uncertainty principle itself   None of this happens without industry  Stefan was direct about it  six industry consortia in the Netherlands  backed by around    million euros in funding  are already developing the vibration free cryocoolers this facility needs  The same technology is finding its way into electron microscopy  superconducting motors for lithography  quantum computing cooling and infrared imaging  And as the project scales toward a multi billion euro facility meant to run for    years  industry brings something physicists don t have on their own  systems engineering  quality assurance and risk management at that level   ET Pathfinder has already drawn    research institutions from   countries  A newly secured    million euro expansion will add larger clean rooms and taller test towers  preparing the ground for a facility Stefan expects will eventually involve around       researchers across Europe   The Einstein Telescope will tell us about the universe  Getting there is being built  quite literally  on light

MUNICH BASED LINQUE CLAIMS ENERGY REDUCTION of    times  In her last contribution as Optica Director of Technology for Optics and Optical Systems  my colleague Dr Olga Raz visited Linque in Munich   Linque is doing something the silicon photonics world has talked about for years  a large scale programmable photonic fabric that routes optical signals on chip  with no optical electrical optical conversions anywhere in the path  Their RISE   optical circuit switch debuted at OFC Conference this year and is now in customer validation  with hyperscalers and neo clouds both at the table   The number that gets attention is the company s claim of   x better energy efficiency than conventional switches  The explanation is simple  in an electrical switch  most of the power goes into SerDes  error correction  and the lasers that regenerate the signal after each conversion  Remove the conversions and that power budget largely disappears   Two things stood out from Olga s conversation with the team  First  they are positioning as a system integrator  not a chip vendor  When asked the build to be acquired question  the answer was direct   we are more of the acquirer   Second  their win at the IC Taiwan Grand Challenge in June  one of    selected from     startups across    countries  opens exactly the foundry and OSAT relationships a photonics company needs to scale   The message Linque left us with applies to the whole industry  photonics reaching product stage in the data center is not a one company story  It takes the full semiconductor value chain  from equipment makers and fabs to OSATs  chip designers and system integrators  moving at the speed this buildout demands

REINDUSTRIALISATION IS NOT about turning the clock back  In a tense geopolitical moment  the easy instinct is to protect legacy industries  The leaders actually building capacity have rejected that groundbreaking in Sherman  Texas  you cannot compete with someone doing what they have done for    or     years  so you look for a transition  a phase shift  a new industry where new skills  new factories and new companies can exist  The plants that were unnecessary or insufficient before  for chips  packaging and photonics  are precisely the ones AI now demands   We have seen this pattern before  Automotive lighting did not defend the headlight  As 艾迈斯欧司朗 CEO Aldo Kamper has described  the value moved to sensing  visualisation and new semiconductor content  Lead  never follow  Photonics and semiconductor leaders understood this early  and they understood something else  in challenging geopolitics  a strong regional strategy is not optional  Jim Anderson is scaling   inch WHAT DID QUIX JUST MAKE OBSOLETE  EVERY PHOTONIC QUANTUM COMPUTER THAT CAME BEFORE IT  That was the claim from Jelmer Renema  co founder and Chief Scientist of QuiX Quantum  at last week s Optica Quantum Industry Summit in Glasgow  collocated this year with Quantum      On the exhibition floor  he announced Carina  which QuiX is calling the first universal photonic quantum computer deployed to a customer site   Universal is the operative word  It means the machine can execute any quantum algorithm  including the famous ones like Shor s and Grover s that require arbitrary quantum computation rather than a narrow set of operations tailored to the hardware  Until now  most of the field has been building algorithms to fit the computer  QuiX is arguing the order should be reversed   The technology that makes this possible  according to Renema  is feed forward  A photonic computer works by sending photons through an optical system  If you can switch that optical system in real time based on what some of the photons are doing  you can steer it toward arbitrary quantum computations  Doing that at the speed of light demands a tight combination of fast electronics  high quality detectors  precise optics  and nonlinear optics  all integrated into a single package  Bringing those components together in a deployed device is what QuiX says makes prior delivered systems obsolete   Carina is NOT a lab demonstration  Renema said it is in production  commercially available  and purchasable today  with cloud access already live through QuiX s website  The design choices are aimed squarely at the AI data center buildout  room temperature operation  modular architecture  and scaling through fiber connections  which positions photonic quantum hardware to ride the same infrastructure wave that is already pulling photonics into data centers   On scaling  Renema was direct about the open problems the Summit kept returning to  losses in fiber to chip coupling and modulator efficiency  His case for optimism is that the hardware requirements can be relaxed through software  He pointed to the long run reduction in qubits needed to run Shor s algorithm  and to a photonics tailored error correction strategy QuiX says outperforms conventional quantum error correction by a factor of four  lowering the cost of the machine   The roadmap from here is utility scale  large systems of interlinked  fiber coupled optical racks on a data center floor  stabilized and controlled by a classical computer alongside them  running real industry workloads  With Xanadu  PsiQuantum  IonQ and others in the room  Renema s summary of the week was blunt  The race is on  and quantum utility is now on the horizon
